abstract: ```text Let $\beta_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[\beta_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+\theta_0})$ for an absolute $\theta_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```
hook: A planar Brownian path's thickened trail has about T/(r^2 (log T)^2) holes on average.
summary: For a Brownian path in the plane thickened by radius r and run to time T, the expected number of holes grows like T divided by r^2 times (log T)^2. The proof gives a matching upper bound and also separates holes in the unbounded part of the complement from those created when cavities split. It builds on a companion paper for the lower bound, and the result gives the order of growth, not an exact constant.
title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
